'''Gerrit Jan van Ingen Schenau''' (13 September 1944, [[Leiden]] &ndash; 2 April 1998, [[Weteringbrug]])<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Beek |first=Peter |last2=Bobbert |first2=Maarten |last3=de Groot |first3=Gert |last4=Hollander |first4=Peter |last5=de Koning |first5=Jos |last6=van Soest |first6=Knoek |last7=Tousaint |first7=Huub |year=1998 |title=Obituary: Gerrit Jan van Ingen Schenau |url=https://doi.org/10.1123/mcj.2.3.278 |journal=Motor Control |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=278-280}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Litsky |first=Frank |date=1998-07-04 |title=Gerrit Jan van Ingen Schenau, clap skate creator, dies at 53 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/07/sports/gerrit-jan-van-ingen-schenau-clap-skate-creator-dies-at-53.html |access-date=2025-07-30 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> was a Dutch biomechanist.  He made large contributions to the field of [[biomechanics]], particularly muscle coordination, [[Bioenergetics|energetics]] of movement, and the functions of [[biarticular muscle]]s.  He focused on [[speed skating]] in particular, and played a significant part in the invention of the [[clap skate]].<ref name=slapxtra>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsci.org/news/news9703/slapxtra.htm|title=Background to the slapskate: Fifteen years of slapskate history, biomechanical backgrounds, first results and recent developments|publisher=sportscience|author=Jos de Koning|year=1997}}</ref>

He died of cancer in 1998.<ref name=":0" />
